requirements.requirement: curl package on node1 is held at its current installed version (7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19) so it will not be changed by a system update
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed curl at 7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19 with no prior hold. `sudo apt-mark hold curl` was applied and verified via `apt-mark showhold` and `dpkg --get-selections curl` (both show 'hold'). Effectiveness was directly demonstrated: after `apt-get update`, a simulated `apt-get upgrade -s` lists many other packages to be upgraded/configured, but curl does not appear in that list, proving the hold prevents curl from being touched by an update.

requirements.requirement: The hold/version persists correctly (not merely applied transiently) and node remains healthy afterward
requirements.summary: Post-restart verification (after an out-of-scope but executed reboot) shows curl still installed at the identical version 7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19, hold status still present in `apt-mark showhold` and dpkg selections, and `curl --version` functioning normally, confirming the hold is durable and the package/node state is healthy.

overall_summary: The task requirement — holding curl at its current version so a system update skips it — is satisfied with direct, positive evidence: the hold was applied, confirmed through two independent mechanisms (apt-mark showhold, dpkg selections), and its effect was proven via a real upgrade simulation that excluded curl while including numerous other packages. Post-restart re-verification shows the hold and version persisted and curl remains functional. The mandatory node-restart protocol (independent of the public contract) was also executed cleanly: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, observed connection loss, a new boot_id, and full post-restart recovery of curl/package state, all cross-checked against the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots which show only the expected boot-identity and boot-scoped temp-file changes and no failed services or package-health regressions.
limitations: The 'after_prepare' phase is an alias of 'before_prepare' (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor change separation relies entirely on the before_prepare vs after_executor comparison.

No independent evidence (e.g., a real `apt-get upgrade` rather than a simulation with `-s`) was captured of a genuine, non-simulated update leaving curl untouched; the simulation is treated as adequate direct evidence per apt's design, but this is a slightly softer proof than an actual upgrade run.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task or protocol purposes: `apt-get update` (prerequisite for a meaningful upgrade simulation), `apt-mark hold curl` (the task itself, retained as required), and `systemctl reboot` (required by the separate provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol, not the public task, but executed cleanly with pre/post state capture and no leftover artifacts beyond expected systemd-private temp dirs tied to the new boot). No unnecessary, abandoned, destructive, or security-weakening mutations were found; package state and services remained healthy across the restart (no failed units, package-health clean before and after).
